## Your own placement {#find-your-own-percentile .smaller .output-8}

::: {.small}
- Rerun `try_spec()` with [the choices that you submitted]{.content-visible when-meta="deck.day"}[the specification that you would defend]{.content-visible unless-meta="deck.day"}, in the cell below[ or in your workspace]{.content-visible unless-meta="deck.short"}: its last line places your estimate on the curve
- The placement counts the specifications of the curve whose estimate lies further below zero than yours. For the reference specification it is `r sum(curve$b_pp < curve_ref$b_pp - 1e-9)`: nothing on the curve lies further below zero, and the logit without covariates ties with it
- The same count places the published result and the five analysts
:::

```{webr}
#| autorun: false
# Type the arguments of your specification; run as it stands, this is the
# reference specification
try_spec()
```

::: notes
Your turn to be placed. Type the arguments of [the choices that you submitted]{.content-visible when-meta="deck.day"}[the specification that you would defend, the one you tried last if you like,]{.content-visible unless-meta="deck.day"} into the cell and run it. The last line of its output is your placement: how many of the sixty-four specifications of the curve have a gap further below zero than yours. For the reference specification it is zero, because nothing on the curve lies further below zero, and the logit without covariates ties with it. Two or three minutes. Every one of you can now say where your estimate stands among sixty-four justifiable alternatives, and that sentence – my estimate sits here among the specifications of the curve, built in this way – is a publishable way to report a robustness check.
:::
